rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=50, grad_clip=0.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.0003, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-11 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-10 hr=0.0, n_iter=100 gave rmse=0.00627 -- with 50/100/200-step fits at 0.00628/0.00627/0.00633, inner-step count is MONOTONE-FLAT and NOT a lever. Iters 1-10 all hr=0, rmse 0.00627-0.00657, all far above baseline 0.00521. (2) FAILURE MODE: plain-UNet N2I regresses to the over-smoothed FBP mean; no edge-preserving structural guard (the bilateral sibling's tight range kernel, hr~0.21, is exactly what this solver lacks). (3) ONE KNOB: relative to iter-6 best reference (lr=3e-4, n_iter=50, c=16), grad_clip 1.0 -> 0.0 (OFF). grad_clip has been pinned at 1.0 all run; breast's 128-view FBP adjoint is far milder than Mayo's 2304-view, so clipping may be needlessly damping the per-image updates. (4) HYPOTHESIS: removing grad-norm clipping lets full-magnitude gradients through, which on the well-conditioned 128-view breast geometry may drive the per-image fit to a sharper solution the clipped runs couldn't reach, lowering rmse. If hr rises, clipping was over-damping. Per the ceiling, more likely the unclipped fit reaches the same over-smoothed FBP-consistent solution (hr=0), since the over-smoothing is set by the TARGET not the step magnitude; grad_clip<=0 still skips nonfinite-grad steps so it stays stable. (5) BUDGET: identical to iter-6 (n_iter=50 fast); ~12 min << 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-12 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: seed variance check (314), lr=1e-4 very gentle, pretrain_steps cap, n_iter=400 high, batch_size up for warm-start.
